summary: Create/verify PagerDuty 'Support Escalations' on-call group + schedules aligned to refreshed escalation playbook
description:
Goal
Ensure the correct PagerDuty group(s), schedules, and escalation policies exist for Support escalations and match the newly published escalation paths/coverage rules. This is required so Support can page the right on-call without bypassing #incidents or creating ad-hoc paging.

Background
During playbook refresh review, we found mismatches between the documented escalation contacts and what Support can actually page in PagerDuty (some services lack a Support-facing escalation policy; some schedules are named inconsistently; after-hours routing unclear).

Scope
- Create or update a PagerDuty escalation policy named “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)” that routes to the correct primary/secondary on-call per playbook.
- Ensure schedules exist and are populated for:
  1) SRE On-Call (customer impact)
  2) Platform On-Call (control plane/auth/SSO/audit logs)
  3) Runtime/Serving On-Call (streaming/runtime regressions) OR confirm SRE is the first hop with defined handoff.
- Verify Support can trigger paging via a single, stable PD target (group/policy), not individual users.
- Confirm coverage windows + handoff rules match the playbook (weekday vs weekend; after-hours expectations; follow-the-sun handoff if applicable).
- Update the internal directory (where Support looks up PD targets) and confirm the target is referenced from Slack bridge template automation.

Out of scope
- Changing actual on-call rotations/ownership beyond aligning naming/routing (those changes belong to Eng leadership).

Dependencies / related work
- INT-332 Update Slack automation for support bridges (should reference the final PD target)
- INT-333 Jira automation SLA reminders + required fields (will nudge to page via PD target)

References
- Confluence (Escalation paths & contacts): sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/escalation-paths-and-contacts-2026.json
- Confluence (Slack bridge conventions): sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/slack-bridge-and-incident-channel-conventions.json
- Confluence (Support SLA vs Eng SLO mapping): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/support-sla-vs-engineering-slo-mapping.json
- Email thread (bridge template + Jira linking): sources/gmail/rafael_mendes/20260210-incident-bridge-template-and-jira-linking.json

Acceptance criteria
1) PagerDuty escalation policy exists and is discoverable to Support as the standard paging target:
   - Name: “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)”
   - Contains at least 2 levels (Primary + Secondary) with defined timeout/ack rules.
2) The policy routes to schedules (not individuals) owned by the right org(s) and matches documented escalation boundaries.
3) The PD policy is tested end-to-end (test incident) and results are documented in a comment (who received page, within what time, any gaps).
4) Support-facing doc/template is updated to reference the policy name (or PD shortlink) consistently.

Risk / notes
- Avoid creating a path that bypasses #incidents for Sev0/Sev1 events; this PD target is intended to get the right responders while following the incident process.
- Some customers are enterprise with strict comms cadence; paging must be reliable to prevent SLA misses.

Requested reviewers
- Rafael Mendes (SRE on-call/escalations owner)
- Priya Natarajan (Platform eng sponsor)
- Owen Phillips (Support incidents SME)

Proposed configuration (draft)
Level 1: SRE On-Call (customer impact) (15 min)
Level 2: Platform On-Call OR Runtime/Serving On-Call depending on tag/triage (15 min)
Level 3: SRE Manager On-Call / escalation (optional; confirm with Rafael)

Open questions
- Do we want separate PD policies per product area (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) or a single Support-facing policy that triages to SRE first?
- Is there an existing “Support Escalations” service/policy we should rename rather than create net-new (to preserve integrations)?
comments: 2026-02-06 (Dev Patel): Creating this as a blocker for playbook adoption. Support currently pages a mix of individuals + an old PD policy that doesn’t match the new routing/coverage. Need a single stable target that matches Confluence escalation paths. Tagging Benji for implementation and Rafael for SRE sign-off.

2026-02-07 (Benji Okafor): Started audit in PagerDuty. Found existing escalation policy “Support-Eng Escalations” pointing to a deprecated schedule (last populated 2025-10). Also found “Platform Primary” schedule exists, “SRE Primary” exists, but no dedicated Runtime schedule. Proposed approach: create new policy “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)” that goes to SRE Primary first, then Platform Primary, then SRE Secondary. Waiting on Rafael to confirm whether Runtime should be separate or handled via SRE triage/handoff.

2026-02-08 (Owen Phillips): +1 to single Support-facing PD target as long as playbook makes clear: if Sev0/Sev1 and broad impact, move to #incidents and let incident commander own. For isolated customer issues, Support can page via PD but still use bridge template + link SUP ticket. Please ensure the PD target name is copy/paste-friendly for macros.

2026-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Confirmed: Support should page SRE first for customer-impacting prod issues; SRE will pull in Runtime/Platform as needed. We should not force Support to decide between Platform vs Runtime at page time. Recommend policy levels: L1 SRE Primary (10–15m), L2 SRE Secondary (10–15m), L3 SRE Escalation (manager) only for P0+ customer impact. Platform Primary should be added as subscriber/notification for specific services via incident process, not as default L2 in the Support policy.

2026-02-11 (Benji Okafor): Implemented new escalation policy draft:
- Policy: “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)”
- L1: SRE Primary (15m)
- L2: SRE Secondary (15m)
- L3: SRE Manager On-Call (30m)
Also created a PD shortlink in internal wiki: pd://support-escalations (internal). Next: run a test page during business hours w/ Rafael + document results. INT-332 can now reference the policy name in the Slack bridge workflow.

2026-02-12 (Benji Okafor): Test completed (13:20 PT): triggered a test incident via PD using the new policy; SRE Primary received page in ~30s, acknowledged in 2m, escalation did not proceed. Verified Support has permission to trigger the policy and can find it via PD search. Remaining: update internal Support directory reference + confirm no legacy policy is used in macros (coordinating with Dev Patel + INT-332).
